title: Choose the visual world
question: Bolder hand, as steered — every earlier card is off the table. Every direction now carries your pinned truth: art-led tiles (AI-generated at save, user-overridable) and glance-and-go legibility. Split-Flap Concourse leads by deal order.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: A Milan–Marseille board for the game table: moods as tall art bands with clacking flap name plates, and every change ripples through a character cascade you cannot miss.
options.viewport: The board is the screen: scene rail as track indicators; 2–8 mood bands, each carrying its generated artwork full-bleed behind a frosted plate, name in condensed white flap caps; the sounding band's lamp burns amber, its crossfade counted down in flap digits; one-shots as art chips with flap keys; STOP ALL sits alone in deliberate empty space.
options.risk: Railway nostalgia is romantic, not the table's own story; the flap texture must serve state, not steal it.

raised.raise: Destructive isolation — STOP ALL sits alone, outline until deliberately focused, nothing near enough to hit by accident.
Magnitude made spatial — crossfade and volume read as physical extent (lit cells, filled band), pan as left-right position, never just a number.
One keyed spine — the hotkey column is the fixed rail every row hangs from; keys are structural, always visible.

options.label: Full-Bleed Feed
options.thesis: The sounding mood owns the whole window as living art; name and fade anchored low in a scrim, every action a glyph on the right rail, the next mood one hard snap away.
options.viewport: The active mood's artwork fills the viewport edge to edge; its name, key, and fade readout anchor low-left in a soft scrim; a right rail stacks stop-all, volume, and mix glyphs; hotkeys snap between moods like a feed flip; one-shots live on a pull-up strip of art tiles.
options.case: Holds audience identification — the feed is the grammar this audience scrolls nightly — but loses product clarity: direct access to 8 named moods and 20 one-shots can't live in a one-item linear snap.
options.risk: Linear feed logic undermines direct selection; beautiful state, slow choosing.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The screen as a living specimen: art tiles locked to a visible construction grid, the sounding mood's name built enormous from its cells.
options.viewport: A faint construction grid tiles the dark screen; mood tiles carry their artwork in strict grid cells; the sounding mood's name sets itself monumental across cells in white while its tile takes the one accent plane; hotkeys are cell coordinates; one-shots as a strict cell grid of art chips.
options.case: Holds product clarity — monumental cell-built type reads across the room — but loses audience identification: Crouwel is design-school canon, not the game table.
options.risk: Designer-insider signifiers; can read as a typography demo wearing a soundboard.

options.label: Graphite Dev Console
options.case: Loses both: it is the tool the developer operates, not the table the GM gathers at — and it is the default every Electron soundboard already ships.
options.kept: Destructive isolation — the panic control sits alone, outline until deliberately focused.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.case: Loses both: almost no GM reads dance notation, and an untrained glance must decode the state in a heartbeat.
options.kept: Magnitude made spatial — duration and level as physical extent, pan as left-right position.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.case: Loses both: scholarly marginalia is the reader's desk, not the table — tiny type is the opposite of glance-and-go.
options.kept: One keyed spine — the hotkey column as the fixed rail everything hangs from.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The straight soundboard grid — dark trigger pads, fader column, transport bar — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A dense grid of square trigger pads, right-hand fader column, transport bar across the top — the arrangement every soundboard ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other soundboard by design.
